problem: Embodied PointGoal navigation agents degrade sharply under visual corruptions such as Spatter, Speckle Noise and Defocus Blur, so existing visual encoders and policies are not robust.
motivation: Real-world deployment involves noisy or corrupted visual input, so robustness of the visual representation matters. The paper starts from the observation that pretraining a ViT with denoising masked modeling, plus a term aligning clean and noisy representations, can yield corruption-robust features for policy learning.
key_idea: Pretrain a ViT visual encoder with Regularized Denoising Masked AutoEncoders (denoising masked modeling plus a bidirectional KL regularizer between clean and noisy image representations), then freeze it for PointGoal policy learning.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract suggests that reducing the clean/noisy representation gap through bidirectional KL yields robustness, and the reported gains are largest under Spatter.
method: Visual module (RDMAE): a ViT encoder is self-supervised pretrained with a denoising masked autoencoding task on corrupted images.
Bidirectional KL regularization: minimizes the bidirectional KL divergence between clean and noisy image representations to close the gap between them.
Frozen encoder: the pretrained ViT is frozen and used to extract robust visual features.
Policy module: a navigation policy is learned on top of the frozen visual features for PointGoal navigation.

setting.backbone: ViT encoder (RDMAE-pretrained, frozen) + learned navigation policy
setting.training_data: Not stated in the abstract; self-supervised pretraining on clean and corrupted images, then policy learning for PointGoal
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (likely with GPS/compass point goal), under visual corruptions
setting.action_space: not stated in the abstract (likely discrete low-level actions)

results: RDMAE-Nav is competitive with SOTAs across visual corruptions. Reported absolute improvements: Spatter +28.2% SR and +23.68% SPL; Speckle Noise +2.28% SR and +6.41% SPL; Defocus Blur +9.46% SR and +9.55% SPL. The abstract does not name the baselines.
limitations: Evaluated only on synthetic visual corruptions, per the abstract; no real-robot results mentioned.
Gains under Speckle Noise are small (+2.28% SR).
The abstract gives no benchmark details, so comparisons could not be verified.
compares_to: SOTA PointGoal navigation agents under visual corruptions
